architectural_context.meaning: Out-of-band hardware access can persist independently of application processor/payload communications; dependent on management power and IPMC/IPMB.
Managed FRU has IPMC, managed chassis supports manager function, managed platform one or more System Managers; not a universal physical hierarchy for all sensing systems.
Chassis Manager function need not be standalone physical entity, may reside on PIC, dedicated element, or distributed.
FRU inventory accessible via IPMC/Chassis Manager; includes vendor, model, serial, revision labels, not observed values.
Management 3.3V_AUX power domain distinct from payload power domain; allows lights-out inventory/control.
CMI vs SMI in-band logical services and IPMB/IPMC out-of-band hardware bus separate transport/roles.
Chassis-wide nonvolatile write protection applies to relevant memory per vendor Certificate of Volatility, not universal data destruction/zeroize.
Edition1.1 defines state diagrams and valid transitions with typical descriptions but no specific normative policies for causing a given operational transition.
Sensor/PIC/module state as determined and supplied by System Manager from management viewpoint; source occurrence not evidence of actual deployed System.
Hardware auth, RTE boot, software auth, composition are logical sequence; implementation details system integrator-defined, but specific SHALLs in §§6.5.4.1–4.4.
Root of Trust may be hardware or software; certification/cryptographic implementation details left to design.

holds.detail: ANSI/VITA 46.11/65.0, HOST Tier-2, IPMI normative command and signaling details are cited but not original-source audited; only C239 inline text inspected.
Observation 6.4-2 cites 16.7-4/-5/-6; Rule 6.4-8 points to Recommendation16.7-1, even though current material is §6.4. Do not silently fix.
Rule 6.4.2-6 cites Table17.5.1; Rule 6.4.2-11 cites Table7.15.2, while local selected VITA specification tables appear as 6.4.2-1/-2; meaning and external original source not reconciled.
Permission 6.4.2-2 and -3 are identical about PIC hosting active Chassis Manager potentially sourcing GDiscrete1; two distinct source occurrences retained.
Rule 6.4.2-20 lacks explicit SHALL/verb; do not infer exact obligation, retain as grammatically incomplete despite the Rule label.
C239 §6.5 explicitly says the specific normative policies for making a particular operational state transition are future work; diagram pathways not Profile SHALLs.

PIC P5 discussion duplicates transition to P2 for different reasons; M5/M6 sections refer to PIC where the target is a Module. Preserve exact inconsistent prose, no repaired native state transition rule.
S0 Off typically unreported and PIC/module P6/M6 manager-agent link unavailable, not proven actual hardware failure; no default 'faulted' display.
2015/2021 source imports, June2023 C239 plus Sep2023 erratum, 2025 S251 snapshot3 distinct; §6.4.2-22 eratta noted on original C239 cover, companion edition not interchanged.

No observed four-case equipment data establishes that specific C239 chassis/PIC/IPMB, Root of Trust, voltage and current sensors, flags, or state machines exist in those systems; source only defines SOSA architecture.
